title: PUT /books/{id} echoes "id":0 instead of the updated book's id
evidence: main.go:248 decodes the request body into a fresh Book (ID zero-valued) and main.go:277 encodes that same value back; book.ID is never assigned from the path id. The path id reaches only the UPDATE statement (main.go:118-122). A client PUTting {"title":..,"author":..} to /books/1 receives {"id":0,...}. main_test.go:162-173 asserts title/author/year/isbn on the update response but never ID, so the tests pass over it.
suggestion: Set book.ID = id before encoding (or re-read the row via store.GetBookByID(id)), and assert the ID in the update test.

title: Error responses are text/plain, not JSON, in a JSON API
evidence: Every failure path uses http.Error (main.go:150,159,171,177,183,199,205,210,223,239,250,257,263,267,273,283,289,294), which writes Content-Type: text/plain. Only the success paths set application/json (main.go:187,214,227,243,276). Status codes themselves are correct (201/200/204/400/404/405/500/503).
suggestion: Add a writeJSONError helper that sets Content-Type: application/json and encodes {"error": msg}.

title: GET /books encodes an empty collection as null instead of []
evidence: main.go:89 declares `var books []Book`, which stays nil when no rows match, and main.go:228 encodes it directly, so GET /books?author=NonExistent returns `null`. main_test.go:334-347 only checks len(books)==0 after unmarshalling, so null passes.
suggestion: Initialise with `books := []Book{}` so the empty case serialises as [].

title: Tests never exercise the production router, and GET /health has no test at all
evidence: prompts/neutral.md asks for tests that demonstrate the implementation meets the requirements. All three tests rebuild their own dispatcher (main_test.go:38-59, 218-226, 282-292) over hard-coded paths, so main.go:143-190's mux, the strconv.Atoi id parsing (main.go:156-161) and every 405 branch are never called. No test issues a request to /health. This accounts for most of the missing 43.8% (test_coverage=0.562).
suggestion: Extract the mux into a newRouter(store) http.Handler and drive the tests through it, adding a /health request.

title: /health handler is duplicated — the production copy is the untested one
evidence: main.go:175-190 serves /health from an inline closure; main_test.go:350-365 declares handleHealth with byte-identical logic. Only the test-local copy is reachable from tests, so the shipped handler is never executed.
suggestion: Move handleHealth into main.go alongside the other handlers and register it, deleting the test-file copy.

title: rows.Err() is never checked after the row-scan loop
evidence: main.go:90-97 iterates rows.Next() and returns books without consulting rows.Err(), so a mid-iteration driver error is silently reported as a short list.

title: ?author= filter does not escape LIKE wildcards
evidence: main.go:77-78 builds `"%"+authorFilter+"%"` for a LIKE clause without an ESCAPE clause, so ?author=%25 (or _) is a wildcard: the filter silently degrades to match-all. The value is still parameterised, so this is not SQL injection.
suggestion: Escape %, _ and the escape char in authorFilter and add `ESCAPE '\'` to the query.

title: go.mod requires testify, which nothing imports, and mislabels go-sqlite3 as // indirect
evidence: go.mod:5-8 requires github.com/stretchr/testify v1.12.1 // indirect and github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3 v1.14.50 // indirect; `grep testify main.go main_test.go` returns nothing, while main.go:12 imports go-sqlite3 directly.
suggestion: Run `go mod tidy` — it drops testify and removes the // indirect marker from go-sqlite3.

title: Nullable year/isbn columns are scanned into non-pointer fields
evidence: The schema (main.go:39-40) leaves year and isbn nullable, but main.go:92 and main.go:107 scan them into int/string, which errors on a NULL. Rows written by this service always supply values, so only externally-inserted rows trip it.
suggestion: Scan into sql.NullInt64/sql.NullString, or declare the columns NOT NULL DEFAULT.

title: Server uses DefaultServeMux with no read/write timeouts or graceful shutdown
evidence: main.go:193 calls http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil); no http.Server with ReadHeaderTimeout/WriteTimeout, and no signal handling to close the store (main.go:140's defer never runs).
suggestion: Construct an explicit http.Server with timeouts and shut it down on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
